messages:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU instability detected in cluster rwd-gpu-prod, severity=high. Multiple nodes reporting DRIVER_RESET / Xid 13 errors and repetitive ECC corrected counts. Autoscaler alerted.
Priya (oncall): acked. I'm on it — switching pager to me. pinging eng-sre + eng-runtime.
Mateo (eng-sre): on my way. first ask — is this a single node or multi-node fanout?
Priya (oncall): looks multi-node, 3 nodes in the same rack: rwd-gpu-prod-12, -13, -14. All showing recent kernel oops + container restarts.
Jin (eng-runtime): seeing elevated VCACHE misses and repeated nvidia driver resets in our runtime logs. Suggest we immediately remove these nodes from the LB and drain.
Sasha (support): any customer-facing impact yet? I'm scanning the CS queue.
Eli (customer-success): we have two customers with tail errors on infer requests past 30s. Flagged but not yet escalated. I'll prep a holding message.
Mateo (eng-sre): doing quick triage: grabbing nvidia logs + dmesg from one node.
Mateo (eng-sre): ```
# tail -n 40 /var/log/kern.log
[172ms] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, GPU has fallen off the bus
[174ms] nvidia-modeset: Loading NVIDIA UNIX x0 driver
[175ms] kernel: NVRM: rm: RmInitAdapter(0) failed, device minor number 255
[176ms] kernel: ECC: corrected errors increased to 512
```
Priya (oncall): Xid 13 + ECC incr — looks like either a hardware flake or driver HW/firmware mismatch. We need a quick mitigation to stop customer impact.
Jin (eng-runtime): mitigation plan proposal: 1) cordon/drain affected nodes, 2) route traffic to GPU-dedicated warmpool and CPU fallback with tokenized rate limiting, 3) scale up spare dedicated nodes in a different AZ. Can do steps 1 and 2 now.
Mateo (eng-sre): running drain for rwd-gpu-prod-12: ```kubectl cordon rwd-gpu-prod-12 && kubectl drain rwd-gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
infra-bot: Action logged: node rwd-gpu-prod-12 cordoned by mateo at 1769505001.
Priya (oncall): confirming routes updated: routed ~40% of requests to fallback model variants, 60% to warmpool. Monitoring error rates.
Sasha (support): updating support threads: "We are aware of GPU infrastructure instability affecting inference latencies for some customers. Mitigation in progress; next update in 30m."
Mateo (eng-sre): gathering ECC stats across nodes: ```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | grep -E "Device|ECC Errors"
Device 0: Tesla-A100-SXM4
  Volatile ECC:  corrected: 1024, uncorrected: 0
Device 1: Tesla-A100-SXM4
  Volatile ECC:  corrected: 2, uncorrected: 0
```
Jin (eng-runtime): weird distribution of corrected counts — one card is spiking. Could be thermal or PCI connectivity. Checking iostat and lspci resets.
Mateo (eng-sre): I see repeated NVLINK messages on the kernel: ```
[...kernel...] nvlink: error: link down, resetting controller
```
Priya (oncall): decision: begin rolling drain of the whole rack (12-14) to avoid cascading OOMs and driver thrash. We'll keep warmpool up in other racks.
Eli (customer-success): notifying two affected customers with an ETA 60-90 mins and offer to move traffic to dedicated sandbox if needed.
vendor-nvidia: Hi team — we saw similar patterns in earlier firmware combos. Please capture full nvidia-smi -q output and driver versions; we'll triage.
Mateo (eng-sre): collected info and uploaded to vendor case: driver 535.86, kernel 6.1.21, firmware PCIe 1.2. Dump uploaded: s3://rwd-artifacts/incidents/1769504823/dumps.tar.gz
Priya (oncall): while vendor looks, we're keeping nodes cordoned and evacuating pods. CPU fallback is handling ~55% of traffic, latency spike down to 2x baseline for affected customers.
Jin (eng-runtime): to reduce driver churn, I'm disabling aggressive autoscaling of GPU pool for 20m and limiting new allocations to warmpool-only. Patch applied: routing-policy: prefer: warmpool, fallback: cpu.
Sasha (support): customers updated. No new escalations so far.
Mateo (eng-sre): next steps: schedule maintenance window to power-cycle affected nodes and run memtest + firmware upgrade if vendor confirms. I'll prepare runbook.
Priya (oncall): handoff to night oncall (Jordan) at 1769507400. Jordan, you have the incident after me; vendor is engaged, we've cordoned 12-14, traffic routed to warmpool/CPU fallback, CS notified.
Jordan (oncall): acked in advance (this is Jordan's calendar slot).
infra-bot: Incident timeline updated; severity remains high.
vendor-nvidia: Thanks — we'll review dump and advise on firmware/driver hotfix. Our initial read: Xid 13 + high corrected ECC suggests intermittent PCIe/thermal issue; firmware upgrade + reseat recommended.
Priya (oncall): logging postmortem stub and tags: root_cause: suspected hw flake/firmware; mitigations: drain/route/fallback; owner: eng-sre; sla_impact: partial degradation for small subset for ~45m.
Mateo (eng-sre): saving logs, will follow up with maintenance plan and ETA for restore.
Eli (customer-success): I'll follow up with customers once we have vendor confirmation.
Priya (oncall): closing active pager for now — still open incident thread for follow-up and postmortem. Will update when nodes are back in service. :white_check_mark:
